learningObjective: Reason about the effect of TensorIR schedule primitives on loop structure and buffer scoping.

canonicalClaims.claim: TensorIR schedule primitives operate on loops and blocks in a semantics-preserving way: `split` divides a loop into an outer/inner pair, `bind` maps a loop to a thread axis, `cache_read`/`cache_write` insert staging buffers at a given storage scope, and `vectorize` marks a loop for target-vectorized codegen when preconditions hold.
conditions: Preconditions of each primitive (e.g., no cross-iteration dependence for `vectorize`) must be met.
nonImplications: Does not imply every schedule improves performance.
Does not imply all primitives succeed on every loop.

misconceptions.claim: `vectorize` always succeeds by silently downgrading to scalar code when preconditions fail.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The scheduler reports an error at schedule-application time when preconditions are violated.
`bind` can be applied to any loop directly; extents just become the thread/block-axis size.

misconceptions.claim: `cache_read` changes the mathematical result by inserting a lossy staging buffer.
Schedule primitives operate on the buffer graph, not on loops.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They operate on the block/loop structure; buffer changes are secondary.

implementationFacts: `split(loop, factors=[None, 256])` binds inner factor 256 and outer becomes ceildiv.
